p: This festival is called "the Season of our Rejoicing,"
for it is written, "In sukkos you shall dwell," etc.,
that I made the Children of Yisrael
And they asked: why was no remembrance made
for the manna and the well,
but only for the Clouds of Glory?
But in truth one must look closely:
if the reason for the sukkah
is a remembrance of the Clouds of Glory,
"so that you remember that in sukkos," etc.,
the day of your going out from the land of Egypt"
Yet it is written, "so that they may know,"
meaning that the knowledge should enter the heart
And this is as we find with Yaakov
on account of "for you have striven
with God and with men, and have prevailed"
That is, at first he was in fear
who is Samael, the evil inclination,
and who appeared to him as a Torah scholar
he touched the hollow of his thigh,
for he still had a claim.
when there was no longer any accusation against him;
then it is written, "And Yaakov journeyed to Sukkos
for Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
was truly made complete in every respect,
as it says, "You will grant truth to Yaakov"
"The lip of truth shall be established forever"
that is, for his children and his descendants,
as we find in the Midrash
that Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him, had
and the number six hundred thousand
is the number of the roots of the souls of Yisrael,
and for this reason they are called "his cattle."
so that at the very least they would merit
And this is the protection from the evil inclination,
"And a sukkah shall be for shade by day," etc.
and it is brought in the Raya Mehemna
"And not in the shade of an ordinary sukkah
that shields the body from the sun,
but a shade to shield the soul."
And this is what it says, "from storm and from rain,"
"He will rain snares upon the wicked"
that is, from all the sins,
as it is written, "And the goat shall bear
'their iniquities' (avonosam) — the iniquities of the wholesome one (tam)."
After this a sukkah is needed
and were it not that the Holy One, blessed be He,
helps him, he could not overcome it.
as it is written, "Light is sown for the righteous"
as it is written, "and for the upright in heart, joy" (ibid.).
a mighty man who conquers his inclination,
and he needs light to shine for him
he still has a struggle and a war,
and he is not in joy.
one who merits to straighten the heart,
לְהוֹרִיק הָרַע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל גַּם כֵּן,
to empty the evil from the "heart of the fool" as well —
And Yaakov merited uprightness of heart
and Yisrael merit it at least
during the days of the festival of Sukkos.
And this is the attribute of da'as,
"He made Yaakov in the mystery of da'as."
And this is what Yisrael merit on Sukkos:
that they merit the attribute of da'as,
"for I made them dwell in sukkos":
And therefore the festival is called "the Season of our Rejoicing."
"Just as the Holy One, blessed be He,
on these days and rejoices in them,
the Holy One, blessed be He, as their portion
For Hashem, may He be blessed, rejoices with Yisrael
for this was the purpose of creation,
לֹא בָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ
"The Holy One, blessed be He, created His world
only so that people would fear Him,
as it says, 'And God has made it so
And at the end of the sixth chapter of Avos (Mishnah 11):
כָּל מַה שֶּׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
"Everything that the Holy One, blessed be He, created
in His world, He created only for His glory."
That is, that the attribute of His Kingship be revealed:
"a king whose awe is upon you"
and Hashem, may He be blessed, has joy
And Yisrael, when they merit uprightness of heart:
whoever is of the holy root
from the war of the evil inclination,
and they rejoice with Hashem, may He be blessed:
And the festival is called "the Season of our Rejoicing."
